messages:
samantha: Heads up — we're getting a burst of 502s and gateway timeouts for hosted inference in eu-west2 (az-b/az-c). Multiple customers on the same routes reporting high latency + failed requests. Escalating now.

matt: saw the anomaly in dashboards ~10:03 UTC, 5xx rate jumped from 0.4% -> 8% for model endpoints in eu-west2. Latency p50/p95 up too.

kevin: looking at edge gateway metrics — retransmit and packet loss spiked on egress paths to provider ASes out of eu-west2-azb. Could be provider side microbursts.

anika: customers 2 and 7 opened support tickets — one mentions auth failures (401 on retry), another mentions billing events showing duplicated attempts. Both saying requests time out before token refresh completes.

julio: quick repro from one customer (they sent):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/llm/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-4b", "prompt":"hello"}' -v --max-time 20
```
They see socket hangups and 502s.

ops-bot: incident-created: INCIDENT-2026-55234 - eu-west2 interconnect saturation affecting hosted inference (assigned: matt, kevin)

matt: early mitigation - throttling ingress on noisy prefixes, enabling cross-region fallback for critical customers (eu-west1 fallback). Pushing config to gateway now.

kevin: ran traceroutes to the affected transit peers, showing asymmetric paths and jumps before packet loss. Pasted sample: 
```
traceroute to 198.51.100.23 (198.51.100.23), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.1.1  0.345 ms 0.289 ms 0.276 ms
 2  203.0.113.45  12.345 ms 12.512 ms 12.498 ms
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.1  120.234 ms 130.456 ms 118.987 ms
```
looks like provider peer flapping after hop 2.

anika: notes on auth — when edge gateway times out we see token refresh race that surfaces as 401s in client logs. Recommend failing fast on token refresh and relying on short-lived fallback tokens we can issue server-side.

julio: support-bot forwarded customer logs — snippet shows repeated 502 then 504s and retries stacking up. Customers complaining about duplicated billing events when retry logic retries charge.

support-bot: customer_2: "We had 40% of requests fail between 10:00-10:20 UTC, then billing recorded 1.7x charges for some requests."

nina: created a short playbook for CS: advise customers to enable regional fallback and set client retry to idempotent-only behavior. Also rolling out a mitigation flag to disable automatic in-line token refresh for affected tenant IDs.

matt: vendor outreach — opened ticket with transit provider (AS64444) with traceroutes attached, asking for QoS logs and interface stats. Also raising BGP community dampening flags to avoid reroutes.

kevin: temporary config change applied: prefer internal peering path via eu-west1 for inference egress, enforcing sticky sessions to avoid cross-AZ hops. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: config-deploy: gateway/policies/egress-prefers-eu-west1 applied at 10:18 UTC by matt (id: cfg-9901).

julio: ask SRE on-call to collect tcpdump on one affected host for 5 minutes: use
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 198.51.100.23 -w /tmp/euw2-probe.pcap -c 20000
```
attach to the incident ticket.

kevin: also collect host-side kernel counters (retransmits, ifconfig) and GPU host network queue stats — create a short script:
```
/sbin/ifconfig eth0 | egrep 'tx|rx|drops|errors'
cat /proc/net/snmp | egrep 'Tcp:|Ip:'
```

anika: CS note — for customers seeing 401s, setting graceful retry backoff to 5s + jitter helps avoid token refresh storms that coincide with network recovery.

matt: early results: after egress pref change errors dropped from 8% -> 1.2% in 7 minutes. Still seeing tail spikes at p99 for some endpoints.

nina: CS update posted to affected customers with mitigation steps, ETA for full provider fix TBD. Include recommended client retry settings and the temporary flag for token refresh.

julio: billing team pinged — asking for list of duplicated-charge candidates so we can reconcile and credit customers proactively.

support-bot: customer_7: "We appreciate the quick fallback. Please confirm when full stability is restored, we saw model hallucination due to truncated responses."

kevin: continuing to monitor BGP and interface counters with provider. If provider can't stabilize within 1 hour we'll trigger planned failover to dedicated capacity for top-tier tenants.

matt: adding closure criteria to incident: sustained 5xx < 0.5% for 30m, provider confirms no microbursts for affected peers, and CS billing reconciliation queued.

samantha: thanks team — keep updates short. If anyone needs escalations to infra-provider legal/ops, ping me directly. :handshake:
